Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. potential for operational transition in Phase 2. This decision will be based upon several factors, including assessments of usability and scalability, the overall system design, a proposed integration and risk mitigation plan for Phase 2, the performer’s ability to assist with technology transition, and the performance of a prototype developed during Phase 1. OM&S assets are not recognized in the Munitions APSR, TICMS, until physically received at an Air Force location. When acceptance is performed by DCMA at a vendor location prior to shipment this creates a period of time during which items are owned by the Air Force but are not included in Air Force financial reporting. The issue is the period of time during which the Air Force is responsible for ownership of an item but has not recorded/acknowledged transfer of ownership to the Air Force. USAF has identified this as an enterprise issue that may affect multiple assessable units (AUs) including but not limited to Munitions, Spare Engines, Base Possessed, Depot Possessed, and Contractor-managed & Possessed.FY21 UpdateDCMA accepts Munitions at the source and then the items are shipped to Army locations and recognized in the Army system LMP.
